name: linetxt
description: Four one-shot text reveals behind one entry point: typing, line-by-line rise, a gentle per-character rise, and a pixel reveal that assembles the glyphs before showing them.

entry.no_default_type: An unset or unknown type throws. The mode is chosen by the user, never inferred silently by the runtime.

typewriter.description: Characters are revealed one after another in DOM order. Layout is final from the first frame; only opacity changes.

charDuration.meaning: Per-character fade length; 0 is a hard cut

caret.meaning: Blinking caret that follows the typing position

caretPersist.meaning: Keep the caret after the last character

caret.layout: Zero-width host span; the bar is an absolutely positioned pseudo-element, so caret movement never reflows text.
caret.clock: Position derives from the same start timestamp as the character reveal.

line-reveal.description: Lines rise from below and fade in, one after another.

stagger.meaning: Delay between the start of adjacent lines

y.meaning: Starting offset below the final position

line_detection.text: Split on newlines in the source text.
line_detection.visual: Group words by rendered offsetTop, so the grouping follows real wrapping at the current width.
line_detection.auto: text when the source contains newlines, otherwise visual.
line_detection.single_line: Resolves to one group and animates as a single element.
line_detection.granularity: Delays are applied per character unit, keyed by the unit's line. No block wrappers are inserted, so host formatting is untouched.

gentle.description: A gentle per-character rise on a frozen motion contract.
gentle.relationship: Enter only. Looping phrase swaps and exit phases are intentionally out of scope for this skill.

pixel.description: The glyphs are sampled into a pixel grid; scattered pixels converge into the letter shapes, hold as pixelated text, then resolve through finer rasters while the real text fades in. No real glyph is visible before the preview completes.

previewDuration.meaning: From the first scattered pixel to fully formed pixelated text

pixelSize.meaning: Cell size; auto is fontSize / 8 clamped to 2–16

scatter.meaning: Radius pixels start scattered from their final cell

revealDelay.meaning: Hold on the pixelated text before it resolves

revealDuration.meaning: Finer rasters, then the crossfade to clean text

easing.meaning: Easing of each pixel's convergence and of the crossfade

timeline.preview: 0 → previewDuration: pixels appear scattered, drift and flicker, then converge on their grid cells, biased toward reading order.
timeline.hold: previewDuration → previewDuration + revealDelay: the coarse pixelated text is held.
timeline.resolve: Next revealDuration ms: raster levels at cell, cell/2, cell/4, then the anti-aliased glyphs; units animate opacity 0 → 1 with delay previewDuration + revealDelay; the overlay fades out over the last 45% and is removed.

sampling.source: Each grapheme unit is drawn into an offscreen canvas at its own DOM box with the host's computed font, colour and text-transform; the baseline is derived from the box height and the font's ascent/descent.
sampling.grid: Alpha coverage is averaged per cell; cells above the ink threshold become pixels with alpha keyed to coverage.
sampling.budget: The cell size grows until the pixel count fits the tuned maximum, so long copy stays smooth.

overlay.element: canvas.linetxt__pixels, aria-hidden, position: absolute, pointer-events: none, z-index -1 inside an isolated host, bleeding past the text box by the scatter radius.
overlay.layout: Never takes part in layout; the units occupy their final boxes from the first frame, so there is no layout shift.
overlay.clock: The overlay's opacity animation is the preview clock; the canvas is repainted from its currentTime each frame.

pixel.tuning: PIXEL_TUNING in linetxt.js: autoSizeDivisor, min/maxPixelSize, maxPixels, inkThreshold, travel, orderBias, drift, decoyRatio, flickerInterval, sampleScale.
pixel.fallback: No 2D canvas or a zero-size host shows the text directly; reduced motion renders static text.

shared.splitting: Grapheme clusters via Intl.Segmenter, with Array.from as the fallback.
shared.grouping: Character units are grouped into non-breaking inline-block word wrappers; trailing whitespace stays with the preceding word.
shared.rise: line-reveal and gentle share one rise implementation and differ only in what the delay is keyed to: line index versus character index.
shared.accessibility: The full text is the host aria-label; every split span is aria-hidden.
shared.lifecycle: play, stop, destroy, finished. destroy restores the original child nodes, aria-label, and classes.
shared.easing: CSS easing strings are shared by every mode; the pixel preview parses keywords and cubic-bezier() into a function for canvas drawing.

waapi.completion: Await animation.finished, apply the final inline frame, then cancel the retained animation.
waapi.pixel: The overlay canvas is repainted by requestAnimationFrame from a WAAPI clock animation; the crossfade is a per-unit opacity animation.

motion.completion: Await the returned controls and stop them during teardown.

gsap.call: Set the first frame with gsap.set, then tween with gsap.to and overwrite: 'auto'.
gsap.completion: Resolve a Promise from onComplete and kill tweens during teardown.

invariants: The mode is supplied by the user; the runtime throws rather than defaulting.
Preserve the application's copy and presentation styles.
Split per grapheme cluster, group into non-breaking word wrappers, wrap only between words.
Expose the full text as the host aria-label and hide split spans from assistive technology.
Render static text when reduced motion is preferred.
Typing must not reflow text: reveal with opacity, never with insertion.
Pixel mode shows no real glyph before the pixel preview completes, samples the actual letter shapes, and leaves plain crisp text with the overlay removed.
Do not add an exit animation unless the user asks for one.
